title: On the trapping of ray families by mirrors
summary: We settle two questions of Serge Tabachnikov regarding the trapping of light rays by mirrors. We show (i) that the largest dimension of a trapped family of rays in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $2n-3$, and (ii) that in $\mathbb{R}^3$ one can trap a 2-parameter family of rays that is not locally normal to any smooth surface. We first establish that no $2n-2$-parameter family can be trapped by showing that no open subset of $L_n$ can be trapped due to Poincaré's recurrence theorem, yielding an upper bound of $2n-3$.
